mode: image2image (vanilla CSFF card art as style reference)
prompt:
Use the attached reference images, each for one purpose.
Reference image 1 is a style reference only: match its flat posterized colour fills, thin dark ink outlines, small ink tick marks and muted palette; do not copy its subject.
Reference image 2 is the SCENE to keep: draw exactly this same stretch of beach seen from above, keeping the grey sky and calm sea at the top, the wide pale tan sand filling the middle and the white curling surf edge sweeping across the lower right, in the same layout and camera position. Change only this: there are far fewer shells.
Reference image 3 shows how the shells look: draw them like these, creamy white shells with thin ink outlines, a fan-shaped ribbed scallop and a white spiral whelk.
Subject: smooth empty sand at the tideline with exactly two white seashells lying on it, one white ribbed scallop shell and one small white spiral shell, a little apart from each other in the middle of the sand. Nothing else lies on the sand.
The sand is smooth and untouched: no footprints, no tracks, no prints of any kind.
Style: Card Survival Fantasy Forest game card art. Flat posterized colour fills in a few hard-edged tonal steps, cel-like, no soft gradients, no watercolour bleed, no paper texture. Thin dark ink outlines and small ink hatch and tick marks for texture. Muted naturalistic palette. Realistic proportions, nothing glossy, no fantasy glow. The painted scene reaches every edge of the frame. No text, no watermark, no signature, no border, no frame.
Avoid: more than two shells, grey shells, brown shells, piles of shells, pebbles, stones, seaweed, footprints, tracks, prints or marks in the sand, birds, gulls, crabs, people, boat, photo, photorealistic, 3D render, anime, pixel art, neon colours, lens flare, watercolour, soft gradients, text, watermark, signature, logo, border, frame, plain white background, vignette, white border.
note: Owner-approved 2026-10-10 in the Card Art Redo Review (second round, redrawn from the owner's notes on the first). Finished by /process-card-art --full-bleed.
